item.title: I work with people with schizophrenia
item.content:encoded:
This SCP is something I find most intriguing. And frightening.

Three questions

Is it literally "genuine" schizophrenics - OR would someone having their brain chemistry getting altered by continuous use of a strong psychotropic like LSD be affected?

Did you know that during an experiment (real world - not SCP universe) using electro-magnetism to effect temporal lobe function, many of the test subjects stated they felt that there was another person/presence in the room with them?

And finally, would it be okay to do an illustration based on this SCP?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is an excellent point. We can't perceive the creatures at all- but judging by the noise from the containment cell, we can perceive the consequences of their actions.

Could the Foundation exploit that? For instance, spray down the interior of the containment cell with paint, or lay a sheet of flexible material over it and attach jingle bells to the sheet. You can't perceive the creature, but you can see paint move. You can't see which way it goes if it tries to escape, but you can see which way the sheet moves. You can't hear its footsteps, but you can hear bells jingle.

Hard to implement when you don't know where the thing is and are trying to operate covertly, but it's a start.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I just realized something; these things have, and I quote, "The perfect camouflage." Which means that no matter what technology you use, like heat signature goggles, the machine would pick up the monster's heat signature, but it would still look invisible. And the only reason we can hear the one contained is not because of the noise it makes, but because of the noise it's containment cell makes when it bangs into it. You can't see, hear, feel, taste, or smell these things (unless you're schizophrenic, of course).

I thought that it was kinda creepy that you can't see them, but then I realized how good this idea is when I realized that you can't even perceive them.

+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Perhaps writing philosophy would have been a better choice of words. The Foundation was more of a collection of the strange and weird in those days. There was a more open attitude to what was acceptable as a skip. Articles tended to be short and sweet and to the point. Now it seems that there is a dismissive attitude to so many different possibilities that used to be explored. I tire of seeing so many promising ideas met with a dismissive "generic magic item" or "X-man". I'm sure that at least some of those ideas could have become excellent skips if they had been encouraged instead of sniffed at. The unrelenting darkness that seems to permeate most articles is becoming slightly depressing to me. This is just my opinion and I still love this wiki and it's writers. Maybe I'm just getting old and wearing my rose colored glasses.

It's interesting, but the unanswered questions I have still prevent me from liking it too much- like, how do researchers know that these aren't schizophrenic hallucinations, or that there aren't multiple types of them that all look different (why go to the assumption that they're one species?) Have non-schizophrenic people seen them eat anything, or turn them into more 870's? How often does this happen, for it not to be noticed in big cities? (Do they wait till the prey are in secluded areas, like their own houses, or not eat plants and such in public?) Do we have any guesses as to why only schizophrenics can see them?

…You probably shouldn't answer all of these directly in the article, but what I mean is, this doesn't sound credible enough for me to be able to run with it. Think about how scientists would approach something like this. And I like the concept a bunch, but I feel like you should expand on it.

item.content:encoded:
Okay, so.

It is currently believed that there could be hundreds, if not thousands, of SCP-870 in the world. They are a clear and present danger to the public, and steps must be taken to destroy or contain the species.

AND YET, somehow, It's Euclid, not Keter.

Standard practice is not to include drawings of SCPs, but then, I guess that's the point? The 5 year old's drawing doesn't seem like something the foundation would bother with.

Aside from that, it's not very interesting.

My initial reaction was kind of "Uugh…" but in retrospect it's not bad. Being perceived only by schizophrenics is interesting, I suppose? The statements that it is incredibly hostile seem like they're trying to play into cheap scares. The very last paragraph is pretty blatant in the "THIS THING IS DANGEROUS, BE FUCKING SCARED. IT COULD BE SNEAKING UP ON YOU RIGHT NOW!"
